description.value:
You have created a set of remotely controlled magical servants called pawns. Each pawn is either Controlled or Inactive. Inactive pawns are inanimate objects and can’t move or act. An Inactive pawn becomes Controlled when its maestro uses the Take Control action.

Take Control ◆

Traits magical, maestro, manipulate

Frequency once per round

You form a magical connection with your pawns, and they become Controlled. Choose any number of Inactive pawns within 10 feet, even if they’re held in a bag or container (as long as it can be opened easily). Each pawn stands up in its space, or in an adjacent space if its own isn’t available, and assumes a battle-ready posture. This doesn’t trigger reactions based on movement. You can’t target a pawn with this ability if it has the broken condition, has 0 Hit Points, or is missing any of its original components.

Controlled pawns function like creatures with the construct and mindless traits, and they can provide flanking. A pawn becomes Inactive if it’s reduced to 0 Hit Points or if its maestro falls unconscious for any reason. A maestro can release control of a pawn at any time as a free action. A Controlled pawn that leaves your Range of Control for any reason immediately becomes Inactive. When a Controlled pawn becomes Inactive, it collapses to the ground in its space.

At 1st level, you can control up to two pawns at a time. This increases to three pawns at 5th level, four at 9th level, and five at 13th level. If you use Take Control while you’re already controlling your maximum number of pawns, choose enough of your Controlled pawns to become Inactive that you don’t exceed your maximum.

While Controlled, each pawn is connected to you by a plainly visible magical phenomenon, such as ethereal strings or beams of light. Normally, this phenomenon can’t be hidden or disguised by any means, and any intelligent creature can infer a relationship between you and your creations. The phenomenon is intangible, passing through or around anything that would obstruct it, and it can’t be attacked or damaged in any way.

Your pawns aren’t minions. They don’t have the minion or summoned trait, and they can act only while under your control. You and your Controlled pawns share your actions and your multiple attack penalty. Each round, you can use any of your actions (including reactions and free actions) either for yourself or for one of your pawns. Pawns can’t speak and have no senses of their own; they rely on your senses for any actions that require them.

Finally, you can also Take Control as an exploration activity to have all your Controlled pawns take move actions as needed to follow you during exploration. While doing so, your pawns must remain within 10 feet of you and can’t take any actions other than actions with the move trait.

Pawns: Additional Rules

Any pawns you create follow these rules unless stated otherwise.

Riding Pawns

In general, a maestro can’t ride their pawns, regardless of the pawns’ size; any attempt to do so causes the pawn to become immobilized. A pawn can carry or drag an ally as long as the pawn is one size larger than that ally, but while doing so, it can move only using its land Speed.

Size

By default, a pawn is a Small creature, and its body is made of 1 Bulk of the materials described in your Craft.

Attribute Modifiers and Proficiencies

Your pawns’ Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution modifiers are equal to half your Intelligence modifier, rounded down. Their Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma modifiers are equal to yours despite their being mindless, because they’re under your influence.

Your pawns’ level is equal to yours. They have expert proficiency in Fortitude, Reflex, and Will saves and are trained in Perception. They’re also trained in unarmed attacks and unarmored defense. They share your skill proficiencies.

Pawns gain an item bonus to AC equal to your Intelligence modifier, with a Dexterity modifier cap of +0. A pawn can use your Intelligence modifier instead of its Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack roll of any Strike it makes.

Hit Points and Healing

By default, a pawn has 10 Hit Points, plus a number of Hit Points equal to 4 + its Constitution modifier for each level you have.

A pawn gains the broken condition whenever it’s reduced to 0 Hit Points. If a pawn becomes broken twice within 10 minutes, it’s destroyed. A pawn loses the broken condition after it has been successfully repaired once using the Repair activity; the DC is the standard DC for your level. With the GM’s approval, you can use a set of artisan’s tools relevant to your Craft for this activity instead of a repair kit. You can also Repair as part of the Refocus activity, performing both at the same time.

Your deep familiarity with your creations’ design lets you mend them more efficiently. When you Repair your pawns, they regain twice the listed number of Hit Points, and you can repair a number of pawns at once equal to the maximum number you can control.

Inactive pawns can still be targeted or affected by attacks and spells; they use their AC, Hit Points, and saving throws as though they were creatures rather than objects. Inactive pawns automatically fail (but don’t critically fail) all saving throws. If a pawn takes any damage while it has 0 Hit Points, it’s destroyed.

Immunities

As constructs, pawns are immune to bleed damage, death effects, disease, healing, nonlethal attacks, poison, vitality, void, and the doomed, drained, fatigued, paralyzed, sickened, and unconscious conditions. As mindless creatures, pawns are also immune to mental effects and mental damage.

Because pawns are neither living nor undead, effects that heal living or undead creatures can’t restore their Hit Points. Restoring a pawn’s Hit Points normally requires the Repair activity or another effect that can restore Hit Points to objects.

Senses

Pawns have no senses of their own. A pawn perceives whatever its maestro perceives, as though it were standing in its maestro’s space. For example, a pawn inside an obscuring cloud of smoke could Strike an opponent that its maestro sees clearly without any penalty. Conversely, if the maestro is blinded, all of their pawns act as though they were also blinded.

Speed

Pawns have a Speed of 25 feet.

Magic Dispelling Effects

Because the connection between a maestro and their pawns is magical, it can be dispelled by effects such as the dispel magic spell. Against such effects, a pawn’s counteract DC is equal to its maestro’s class DC, and its counteract rank is equal to half its maestro’s level, rounded down. If a pawn’s magic is dispelled, the pawn becomes Inactive and falls to the ground without taking any damage other than damage from the dispelling effect itself, if any.

Lost and Altered Actions

Pawns are immune to effects that would change the number of actions they receive each turn, such as slowed, stunned, or quickened, because their ability to act comes entirely from their maestro. If you receive such an effect, it also applies to the actions you share with your pawns. If you or one of your pawns becomes restricted in how you can act, that restriction isn’t automatically shared between you. For example, if your pawn became immobilized or petrified, it couldn’t move, but you could still use your actions to move. The GM resolves any unclear situations.

Creating New Pawns

You can create a new pawn from the equivalent Bulk of the materials specified in your Craft. Creating a single pawn takes 1 hour of work: sculpting appendages, carving runes, or performing special rites, as appropriate. You need a flat surface and an appropriate set of tools to do this. Pawns don’t benefit from any special properties of the materials they’re made from, such as duskwood or cold iron. A pawn can be used only by the maestro who created it.

Pawns and Equipment

Your pawns can’t wear or wield items, except for items with the pawn trait. Any item that requires investment must be invested by the pawn’s maestro instead, and it counts against the maximum number of items that maestro can invest. Your connection to your pawns lets them benefit from certain magic items you’ve invested.

  • Your Controlled pawns gain item bonuses to skills from any magic items you’ve invested.
  • Your Controlled pawns’ item bonus to AC increases based on the armor potency rune on your armor or on your bands of force. They also gain an item bonus to saves from the resilient rune on your armor or from your bands of force. Other permanent items that grant or increase item bonuses to AC and saves might convey a similar benefit, at the GM’s discretion.
  • Your Controlled pawns’ Strikes benefit from the fundamental and property runes on your handwraps of mighty blows. Alternatively, you can invest a magic weapon (even though magic weapons can’t normally be invested) to share its fundamental and property runes with your pawns. You share these benefits only while you’re holding the weapon, and you can have only one weapon invested this way at a time. In either case, your pawns gain only the benefits that can apply to their attacks, with the same limitations noted in handwraps of mighty blows.

Number of Inactive Pawns

There’s no set limit to the number of Inactive pawns a maestro can have. Each Inactive pawn is its own item, with a Bulk equal to that of the materials needed to create it.
